title: Scala 2.9 support added
source_quote: This is the first release to support Scala 2.9 in addition to 2.8. Future releases are likely to be 2.9-only unless there is high demand for 2.8.

title: Save distributed datasets to HDFS/S3/Hypertable and other Hadoop-supported storage
source_quote: You can now save distributed datasets to the Hadoop filesystem (HDFS), Amazon S3, Hypertable, and any other storage system supported by Hadoop.

title: Native types for common Writable types in SequenceFiles
source_quote: Spark will now let you use native types for certain common Writable types, like IntWritable and Text.

title: Maven-based dependency fetching and artifact publishing
source_quote: Spark now fetches dependencies via Maven and can publish Maven artifacts for easier dependency management.

title: Faster broadcast and shuffle algorithms
source_quote:
This release includes broadcast and shuffle algorithms from
this paper
to better support applications that communicate large amounts of data.

title: SparkContext.hadoopRDD for non-filesystem Hadoop input formats
source_quote:
The new
SparkContext.hadoopRDD
method allows reading data from Hadoop-compatible storage systems other than file systems, such as HBase, Hypertable, etc.

title: Outer join operators added
source_quote:
Outer join operators (
leftOuterJoin
,
rightOuterJoin
, etc).

title: Scala 2.9 interpreter features supported
source_quote: Support for Scala 2.9 interpreter features (history search, Ctrl-C current line, etc) in the 2.9 version.

title: Better default parallelism levels for various operations
source_quote: Better default levels of parallelism for various operations.

title: Ability to control number of splits in a file
source_quote: Ability to control number of splits in a file.

title: Runs on Apache Mesos 0.9
source_quote:
This release runs on
Apache Mesos 0.9
, the first Apache Incubator release of Mesos, which contains significant usability and stability improvements.

title: Mesos 0.9 usability gains: memory accounting, job trace/log history, simpler install
source_quote: Most notable are better memory accounting for applications with long-term memory use, easier access of old jobs’ traces and logs (by keeping a history of executed tasks on the web UI), and simpler installation.

title: Scheduling made more communication-efficient for large lineage graphs
source_quote: scheduling is more communication-efficient when sending out operations on RDDs with large lineage graphs.

title: Improved cache replacement policy
source_quote: the cache replacement policy has been improved to more smartly replace data when an RDD does not fit in the cache

title: Shuffles made more efficient
source_quote: shuffles are more efficient

title: Configurable closure serializer
source_quote: the serializer used for shipping closures is now configurable, making it possible to use faster libraries than Java serialization there.

title: Worker exceptions reported back to master log
source_quote: Spark now reports exceptions on the worker nodes back to the master, so you can see them all in one log file.

title: Automatic marking/filtering of duplicate errors
source_quote: It also automatically marks and filters duplicate errors.

title: New operators: sortByKey, takeSample, faster fold/aggregate
source_quote:
These include
sortByKey
for parallel sorting,
takeSample
, and more efficient
fold
and
aggregate

title: Join of identically hash-partitioned RDDs avoids network shuffle
source_quote:
more of the old operators make use of, and retain, RDD partitioning information to reduce communication cost. For example, if you
join
two hash-partitioned RDDs that were partitioned in the same way, Spark will not shuffle any data across the network.

title: EC2 launch scripts bundled with release and auto-discover latest AMI
source_quote: EC2 launch scripts are now included in the main package, and have the ability to discover and use the latest Spark AMI automatically instead of launching a hardcoded machine image ID.

title: New Hadoop API (org.apache.mapreduce) read/write support
source_quote:
You can now use Spark to read and write data to storage formats in the new
org.apache.mapreduce
packages (the “new Hadoop” API).

title: Spark published to Maven Central
source_quote: Spark is now available in Maven Central, making it easier to link into your programs without having to build it as a JAR.

title: Builds against Scala 2.9.2 by default
source_quote: Spark now builds against Scala 2.9.2 by default.

title: New Accumulable class generalizes Accumulators for non-matching element/accumulated types
source_quote: The new Accumulable class generalizes Accumulators for the case when the type being accumulated is not the same as the types of elements being added (e.g. you wish to accumulate a collection, such as a Set, by adding individual elements). This interface is also more efficient in avoiding the creation of temporary objects.

title: Improved object size estimation for memory management (32/64-bit pointers)
source_quote:
algorithm for estimating the sizes of objects (in order to manage memory correctly) has been improved
    to handle JVMs with 32- vs 64-bit pointers and to measure objects more accurately.

title: Improved random sampling algorithm to avoid bias
source_quote: Improved algorithms for taking random samples out of datasets to avoid biases that could occur in the previous ones.

title: Improved load balancing across nodes in sort operations
source_quote: Improved load balancing across nodes in sort operations.

title: Reduced memory consumption of saveAsObjectFile for large objects
source_quote:
Reduced memory consumption of
saveAsObjectFile
when objects are large.

title: EC2 launch script auto-configures memory limit from instance RAM
source_quote: EC2 launch script now configures Spark’s memory limit automatically based on the machine’s available RAM.

title: Compile support for Hadoop 2 distributions
source_quote: Spark 0.5.2 is a minor release, whose main addition is to allow Spark to compile against Hadoop 2 distributions.

title: Standalone deploy mode added
source_quote:
Spark now has a
standalone deploy mode
that lets you quickly launch a cluster without installing an external cluster manager.

title: Experimental YARN support
source_quote:
there is
experimental support for running on YARN

title: Java API layer added
source_quote:
Java programmers can now use Spark through a new
Java API layer

source_quote: scheduler and control plane have been optimized to better support ultra-low-latency jobs (under 500ms) and high-throughput scheduling decisions.

title: Per-RDD storage level control via persist()

persist()
method

title: New Accumulable class for accumulating collections/mismatched types
source_quote: A new Accumulable class generalizes Accumulators for the case when the type being accumulated is not the same as the types of elements being added (e.g. you wish to accumulate a collection, such as a Set, by adding individual elements).

title: Dynamic file/JAR shipping via SparkContext.addFile/Jar

SparkContext.addFile/Jar

title: More operators (e.g. joins) support custom partitioners
source_quote: More Spark operators (e.g. joins) support custom partitioners.

title: Log now records which program operation produced each RDD/job for easier debugging

title: Spark published to Maven Central

source_quote: PySpark supports most Spark features, including RDDs, accumulators, broadcast variables, and HDFS input and output.

map
,
filter
,
reduce

spark.ui.port
property.

values

subtract

coalesce
,
zip

source_quote:
RDD.toDebugString()

source_quote: Several performance improvements to shuffles.

title: Standalone deploy spreads jobs across machines for better data locality
source_quote: Standalone deploy cluster now spreads jobs out across machines by default, leading to better data locality.

title: Better error reporting when jobs cannot launch due to insufficient resources
source_quote: Better error reporting when jobs aren't being launched due to not enough resources.

title: Standalone web UI adds JSON endpoints for cluster state
source_quote: Standalone deploy web UI now includes JSON endpoints for querying cluster state.

title: Better support for IBM JVM
source_quote: Better support for IBM JVM.

title: Default Hadoop version dependency updated to 1.0.4
source_quote: Default Hadoop version dependency updated to 1.0.4.

title: Improved failure handling and error message reporting
source_quote: Improved failure handling and reporting of error messages.

title: Separate configuration for standalone daemons vs user applications
source_quote: Separate configuration for standalone cluster daemons and user applications.

title: Scheduler codebase refactored to enable richer unit testing
source_quote: Significant refactoring of the scheduler codebase to enable richer unit testing.

title: SparkFiles.getRootDirectory/SparkFiles.get for locating shipped files

you can find the directory it used using

title: Scala version updated to 2.9.3
source_quote: Scala version updated to 2.9.3.

source_quote: Several improvements to Bagel, including performance fixes and a configurable storage level.

title: New API methods: subtractByKey, foldByKey, mapWith, filterWith, foreachPartition
source_quote: New API methods: subtractByKey, foldByKey, mapWith, filterWith, foreachPartition, and others.

source_quote: A new metrics reporting interface, SparkListener, to collect information about each computation stage: task lengths, bytes shuffled, etc.

title: Support for launching multiple worker instances per host in standalone mode
source_quote: Support for launching multiple worker instances per host in the standalone mode.

source_quote:
Users of
spark-shell
can now set the
ADD_JARS
environment variable to add a list of JARs to their clusters; these will also be sent to workers.

source_quote: Spark standalone clusters now properly kill executors when a job ends or fails. In addition, adding JAR paths with backslashes will now work correctly.

source_quote: The Kafka and Twitter APIs for Spark Streaming have been updated. In the Twitter case, this is to deal with the username/password authentication method being disabled in by Twitter, while in the Kafka case, it is to allow receiving messages other than strings.

title: Faster Python VM spawning for large JVM heap sizes
source_quote: mechanism for spawning Python VMs has been improved to do so faster when the JVM has a large heap size, speeding up the Python API.

title: Better error reporting for non-serializable exceptions and large task results
source_quote: Better error reporting for non-serializable exceptions and overly large task results.

title: Spark Streaming build no longer depends on Twitter4J repo
source_quote: Spark Streaming no longer depends on the Twitter4J repo, which should allow it to build in China.

title: Web UI for monitoring at port 4040
source_quote: Spark now displays a variety of monitoring data in a web UI (by default at port 4040 on the driver node).

title: Job dashboard with percentile stats for task runtime, shuffle, GC
source_quote: A new job dashboard contains information about running, succeeded, and failed jobs, including percentile statistics covering task runtime, shuffled data, and garbage collection.

title: Extended storage dashboard with per-executor storage/task pages
source_quote: The existing storage dashboard has been extended, and additional pages have been added to display total storage and task information per-executor.

title: New metrics library exposing internal metrics via JMX and Ganglia
source_quote: Finally, a new metrics library exposes internal Spark metrics through various APIâs including JMX and Ganglia.

title: MLlib machine learning library introduced
source_quote: This release introduces MLlib, a standard library of high-quality machine learning and optimization algorithms for Spark.

title: MLlib ships seven algorithms (SVM, logistic regression, linear regression variants, KMeans, ALS)
source_quote: The current library contains seven algorithms, including support vector machines (SVMs), logistic regression, several regularized variants of linear regression, a clustering algorithm (KMeans), and alternating least squares collaborative filtering.

title: Python API extended with storage levels, sampling, and missing RDD operators
source_quote: The Python API has been extended with many previously missing features. This includes support for different storage levels, sampling, and various missing RDD operators.

title: PySpark support for IPython (incl. Notebook) and Windows
source_quote:
also added support for running Spark in
IPython
, including the IPython Notebook, and for running PySpark on Windows.

title: YARN support improved and promoted from experimental to mainline
source_quote: Spark 0.8 add greatly improved support for running standalone Spark jobs on a YARN cluster. The YARN support is no longer experimental but now part of mainline Spark.

title: Support for running against a secured YARN cluster
source_quote: Support for running against a secured YARN cluster has also been added.

title: Job scheduler refactored with fair scheduler for multi-user sharing
source_quote:
internal job scheduler has been refactored and extended to include more sophisticated scheduling policies. In particular, a
fair scheduler
implementation now allows multiple users to share an instance of Spark, which helps users running shorter jobs to achieve good performance, even when longer-running jobs are running in parallel.

title: Topology-aware scheduling extended: rack locality and multiple executors per machine
source_quote: Support for topology-aware scheduling has been extended, including the ability to take into account rack locality and support for multiple executors on a single machine.

title: Link to Spark for any Hadoop version via hadoop-client dependency
source_quote:
User programs can now link to Spark no matter which Hadoop version they need, without having to publish a version of
spark-core
specifically for that Hadoop version.

title: EC2 scripts support any availability zone and HVM instance types
source_quote: EC2 scripts now support launching in any availability zone. Support has also been added for EC2 instance types which use the newer âHVMâ architecture. This includes the cluster compute (cc1/cc2) family of instance types.

title: EC2 support for running newer HDFS versions alongside Spark
source_quote: also added support for running newer versions of HDFS alongside Spark.

title: EC2 ability to launch clusters with maintenance releases of Spark
source_quote: added the ability to launch clusters with maintenance releases of Spark in addition to launching the newest release.

RDDs can now manually be dropped from memory with
unpersist

takeOrdered
,
zipPartitions
,
top

source_quote:
JobLogger
class has been added to produce archivable logs of a Spark workload.

title: RDD.coalesce now takes locality into account
source_quote:
RDD.coalesce
function now takes into account locality.

title: RDD.pipe supports passing environment variables to child processes
source_quote:
RDD.pipe
function has been extended to support passing environment variables to child processes.

title: Hadoop save functions support optional compression codec
source_quote: functions now support an optional compression codec.

title: Binary distribution depending only on a Java runtime
source_quote: You can now create a binary distribution of Spark which depends only on a Java runtime for easier deployment on a cluster.

title: Examples build isolated from core build to reduce dependency conflicts
source_quote: The examples build has been isolated from the core build, substantially reducing the potential for dependency conflicts.

title: Streaming Twitter API updated to use OAuth authentication
source_quote: The Spark Streaming Twitter API has been updated to use OAuth authentication instead of the deprecated username/password authentication in Spark 0.7.0.

title: Various optimizations to PySpark and the job scheduler
source_quote: This release includes various optimizations to PySpark and to the job scheduler.

title: YARN 2.2+ support added
source_quote: Support has been added for running Spark on YARN 2.2 and newer.

source_quote: Efficient encoding for JobConfs - improves latency for stages reading large numbers of blocks from HDFS, S3, and HBase

source_quote: Shuffle file consolidation (off by default) - reduces the number of files created in large shuffles for better filesystem performance.

source_quote: Torrent broadcast (off by default) - a faster broadcast implementation for large objects.

source_quote: Support for fetching large result sets - allows tasks to return large results without tuning Akka buffer sizes.
